# Generate DLNM Predictions from `GHRmodels` Objects

## Description

This function takes an object of class `GHRmodels`, extracts the relevant coefficients and variance-covariance matrix, and then calls `dlnm::crosspred` to compute predictions over a range of covariate values (or at specified points).

```r
crosspred_inla(
  models,
  basis,
  mod_id,
  at = NULL,
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  lag,
  bylag = 1,
  cen = NULL,
  ci.level = 0.95,
  cumul = FALSE
)
```

## Arguments

- `models`: An object of class `GHRmodels`, containing fitted model output (e.g., `$fixed` and `$vcov` lists).
- `basis`: A cross-basis or one-basis object created by `crossbasis_inla` or `onebasis_inla`.
- `mod_id`: An integer or character string specifying which model within the input `GHRmodels` object to use (e.g., if `model$fixed` and `model$vcov` both have multiple entries).
- `at`: A numeric vector of values at which to compute predictions (e.g., `seq(10, 25, by = 0.2)`).
- `from, to`: Numeric values specifying the range of the prediction sequence if `at` is not specified (e.g., `from = 10` and `to = 25`).
- `by`: Numeric increment for the sequence if `at` is not specified (e.g., `by = 0.2`).
- `lag`: An optional vector of two elements with min and max lag. If missing (default), it uses the same lag structure as defined in `crossbasis_inla`.
- `bylag`: Numeric increment for lag steps (default is 1).
- `cen`: A centering value (e.g., a reference exposure level).
- `ci.level`: The credible interval level (default `0.95`).
- `cumul`: Logical; if `TRUE`, cumulative predictions are computed (default `FALSE`).

## Details

The function identifies which coefficients in `models$fixed[[mod_id]]` and which rows/columns in `models$vcov[[mod_id]]` correspond to the one-basis or cross-basis terms (i.e., matching the column names in `basis`).

Then it passes these slices to `dlnm::crosspred` to generate predictions. The centering value (`cen`), if specified, indicates the reference exposure (e.g., a mean temperature) at which to center the effect estimates (e.g., the effect a given temperature value on the outcome will be compared to the effect of the centering value on the outcome, in this case the mean temperature).

Credible intervals are not obtained by drawing from the joint posterior of the fixed effects. Instead, `dlnm::crosspred` combines the posterior mean coefficients with the posterior covariance matrix (`models$vcov`, itself INLA's Gaussian approximation to the joint posterior of the fixed effects), then builds a symmetric interval as fit `\pm` a Gaussian quantile times the propagated standard error. This is equivalent to a posterior-sampling-based interval as long as the joint posterior of the fixed effects is itself approximately Gaussian and does not reflect any skewness in the individual marginal posteriors.

## Returns

An object of class `"GHRcrosspred"`, inheriting from `"crosspred"`, with fields for the predicted values, credible intervals, and optionally cumulative predictions, as determined by crosspred .

## See Also

`dlnm::crosspred` for details on how predictions are computed.

## Examples

```r
# Load example GHRmodels object from the package
model_dlnm_file <- system.file("examples", "model_dlnm.rds",
                               package = "GHRmodel")
model_dlnm <- readRDS(model_dlnm_file)

# Load example cross-basis matrix from the package: 2-dimensional
# cross-basis matrix of the non-linear effect of dengue risk across
# tmin values and lags:
cb_tmin_file <- system.file("examples", "cb_tmin.rds", package = "GHRmodel")
cb_tmin <- readRDS(cb_tmin_file)

# Generate predictions
pred_result <- crosspred_inla(
  models = model_dlnm,
  basis = cb_tmin,
  mod_id = "mod3",
  cen = 20
)

# Inspect predictions
pred_result$predvar  # the sequence of 'at' values
pred_result$allfit   # fitted values
pred_result$alllow   # lower CI
pred_result$allhigh  # upper CI
```
